outdoor.name: Crissy Field (East Beach), San Francisco
outdoor.note: A flat, stroller-friendly bayfront beach and promenade in the Presidio with calm water, picnic tables, and Golden Gate Bridge views, right next to the giant Outpost playground at Presidio Tunnel Tops.

shopping.name: Ferry Building Marketplace
shopping.note: A historic waterfront marketplace on the Embarcadero with a year-round Ferry Plaza Farmers Market (Tue/Thu/Sat) and kid-friendly food stalls, making for an easy, walkable family stroll.

museum.name: Exploratorium
museum.note: A hands-on science museum on Pier 15 with 650+ touch-test-and-build exhibits, including sections designed specifically for toddlers and young kids.

outdoor.name: Santa Monica State Beach & Pier
outdoor.note: A classic, easy-access ocean beach with soft sand near the pier, plus carousel and Pacific Park amusement rides right on the sand for young kids.

shopping.name: Third Street Promenade, Santa Monica
shopping.note: A car-free, flat pedestrian shopping street just blocks from the pier with street performers and casual dining, easy to navigate with a stroller.

museum.name: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County
museum.note: Home to a stroller-friendly Dinosaur Hall and a live Insect Zoo with docent feeding demonstrations that are a hit with young kids.

confidence_notes: We initially considered the California Science Center (Space Shuttle Endeavour) for this slot, but verified its Endeavour pavilion is currently closed while the shuttle is installed in a new building reopening Nov 13, 2026 (after today's date). Substituted the Natural History Museum of LA County, confirmed fully open now.

outdoor.name: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk (Luna Park)
outdoor.note: A real Atlantic Ocean beach with a historic boardwalk and Luna Park's kid-friendly rides right on the sand, confirmed open daily for the 2026 summer season.

shopping.name: Union Square Greenmarket
shopping.note: A lively year-round farmers market (Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat, 140+ vendors) with a playground right in the square, great for an easy family browse.

museum.name: American Museum of Natural History
museum.note: Iconic dinosaur halls plus a dedicated Discovery Room with hands-on activities and real fossils for ages 4-12, open weekends via free timed passes.

outdoor.name: North Avenue Beach
outdoor.note: A wide, sandy Lake Michigan beach in Lincoln Park with lifeguards in season, a playground, and the landmark ship-shaped beach house, ideal for a family beach day.

shopping.name: The Magnificent Mile (Michigan Avenue) at Water Tower Place
shopping.note: An iconic shopping strip anchored by Water Tower Place, home to American Girl Place and a LEGO Store, both confirmed still operating and big draws for kids.

museum.name: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry (MSI)
museum.note: One of the country's largest science museums, with hands-on exhibits like the U-505 submarine tour and areas built for young children's play and discovery.

confidence_notes: Formerly known simply as the 'Museum of Science and Industry'; renamed the Kenneth C. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry in 2024 after a major donation, and still commonly called 'MSI' -- used both names in the listing for recognizability.

outdoor.name: Klyde Warren Park
outdoor.note: A 5.2-acre deck park in downtown Dallas with the Sheila & Jody Grant Children's Park -- a climbing tower, water features, and play equipment -- plus rotating food trucks, all free to enjoy.

shopping.name: Southlake Town Square
shopping.note: A walkable, courthouse-square-style shopping district with a central fountain kids can splash in, family-friendly boutiques, and a seasonal splash pad nearby at Bicentennial Park.

museum.name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
museum.note: Its newly renovated Moody Family Children's Museum (reopened 2025) is purpose-built for kids 7 and under, with a Makery, an Imaginarium, and an outdoor climbing and water-play area.

confidence_notes: DFW has no iconic ocean/lake swim beach close to the metro core, so a standout park (Klyde Warren) was used for the outdoor slot, consistent with the brief's fallback guidance.

outdoor.name: The Commons at Hermann Park
outdoor.note: A free, shaded two-acre play area inside Houston's flagship park with a nature-themed splash pad, a 45-foot rocket-ship playground, paddle boats, a mini train, and a carousel.

shopping.name: Rice Village
shopping.note: A walkable, boutique-lined shopping village near Rice University with multiple dedicated toy stores (Fundamentally Toys, Learning Express Toys) and easy family dining options.

museum.name: Children's Museum Houston
museum.note: Fourteen bilingual, interactive galleries (water play, a kid-run pretend city, a climbing tower) built for ages 0-12, with free Family Night every Thursday 5-8pm.

outdoor.name: Smithsonian National Zoo
outdoor.note: A free, stroller-friendly walk through wooded paths to see giant pandas Bao Li and Qing Bao and other animals -- an easy, iconic outdoor family outing (free timed-entry passes required).

shopping.name: Eastern Market
shopping.note: A historic Capitol Hill market with fresh food vendors and a weekend outdoor flea/arts market, plus a playground two blocks away, great for a family wander.

museum.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
museum.note: Free entry with a hands-on O. Orkin Insect Zoo and the Q?rius Jr. Discovery Room, a space designed specifically for preschool-age children.

outdoor.name: Centennial Olympic Park (Fountain of Rings)
outdoor.note: A free, zero-depth interactive splash fountain in the heart of downtown, with choreographed water shows four times daily, 365 days a year, right next to Atlanta's other big family attractions.

shopping.name: Ponce City Market
shopping.note: A restored historic Sears building turned food hall and shops along the Atlanta Beltline, with a rooftop mini-golf and carnival-games area (Skyline Park) that's a hit with kids.

museum.name: Children's Museum of Atlanta
museum.note: Six permanent hands-on learning zones plus a rotating feature exhibit (a Wild Kratts ocean-themed exhibit runs May-Sept 2026) make it a strong pick for toddlers through early elementary kids.

confidence_notes: Ponce City Market itself is free to enter and browse; the rooftop Skyline Park mini-golf/carnival-games area requires a separate paid ticket (roughly $15 adult / $7 kids ages 4-12), so the pin description should frame it as the market/food hall stroll rather than implying Skyline Park is free.

outdoor.name: Franklin Square
outdoor.note: One of Philadelphia's historic squares reborn as a family hub with a year-round carousel, a Philly-themed mini-golf course, and a free, award-winning playground open daily.

shopping.name: Reading Terminal Market
shopping.note: America's top-rated public market (2026 USA Today Readers' Choice) with 80+ food and craft vendors under one historic roof — an easy, weather-proof family stroll with something for every age.

museum.name: Please Touch Museum
museum.note: Purpose-built for children under 10 with fully hands-on, permission-to-touch exhibits throughout; located in Fairmount Park's historic Memorial Hall.

confidence_notes: Please Touch Museum's exact weekly operating hours vary by source/season (a couple of listings mention Monday closures) — the venue is confirmed open and operating in 2026, but double-check current hours before publishing anything time-specific.

outdoor.name: Crandon Park Beach
outdoor.note: Two miles of calm, shallow Biscayne Bay shoreline on Key Biscayne make this a local favorite family beach, plus a beachfront playground, splash fountain, and a vintage weekend carousel.

shopping.name: Lincoln Road Mall
shopping.note: A mile-long, tree-shaded pedestrian promenade in Miami Beach with shops, cafes, and a year-round Sunday farmers/green market — flat and stroller-friendly.

museum.name: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
museum.note: A three-level aquarium, dome planetarium, and hands-on exhibits plus a full calendar of family workshops, camps, and occasional family sleepover nights make this downtown Miami museum a standout for kids.

confidence_notes: Crandon Park's vintage carousel and roller rink (Family Amusement Center) run weekends/holidays only; the beach itself, playground, and splash fountain area are open daily, so the pick works as an everyday itinerary stop regardless.

outdoor.name: Encanto Park
outdoor.note: A shaded, 222-acre park built around a fishing lagoon with paddle boats and the Enchanted Island mini amusement park (rides sized for ages 1-10) — its tree cover and water features make it more bearable on hot Phoenix mornings than most outdoor options.

shopping.name: Kierland Commons
shopping.note: An open-air, upscale shopping district in Scottsdale with a splash fountain running daily that doubles as a play spot for kids while parents browse.

museum.name: Children's Museum of Phoenix
museum.note: Three floors of hands-on exhibits (a giant climber, noodle forest, art studio, pretend market) built for babies through age 10, housed in a historic downtown schoolhouse.

confidence_notes: Given extreme Phoenix summer heat, the pin copy should suggest an early-morning visit to Encanto Park; shaded ramadas and the lagoon help but mornings are still notably more comfortable.

outdoor.name: Revere Beach
outdoor.note: America's first public beach (established 1896) is a three-mile crescent of sand with calm, reef-moderated surf, summer lifeguards, and an easy ride via the MBTA Blue Line, making it a low-stress family beach day near Boston.

shopping.name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace & Quincy Market
shopping.note: This historic marketplace packs 40+ shops and a lively food hall alongside free daily street performers (11am-9pm), giving kids plenty to watch while parents browse.

museum.name: Boston Children's Museum
museum.note: A purpose-built, waterfront children's museum with hands-on exhibits designed specifically for young kids, including the perennial Bubbles exhibit and a seasonal Hundred Acre Wood installation (through Sept 2026).

confidence_notes: All three venues confirmed currently operating via 2026 sources (official sites, local guides, and news coverage).

outdoor.name: Coronado Beach
outdoor.note: Consistently ranked one of the best family beaches in North America, this wide, clean, calm beach offers free parking and a stroller-friendly walkable town just steps away.

shopping.name: Liberty Public Market (Liberty Station)
shopping.note: A lively, converted-naval-base public market with 30+ food and specialty vendors and generous outdoor seating gives kids room to roam while parents graze, open 7 days a week.

museum.name: The New Children's Museum
museum.note: A downtown, art-focused children's museum built around immersive, room-sized interactive installations (like a giant pillow-and-mattress climbing space) made specifically for kids.

confidence_notes: Seaport Village, a well-known waterfront alternative for the shopping slot, is technically still open but is in the middle of a long-term (5-9+ year) redevelopment process, so Liberty Public Market was chosen as the more stable evergreen pick instead.

outdoor.name: Ala Moana Beach Park
outdoor.note: A reef-protected lagoon at Magic Island keeps the water calm and shallow, and shaded lawns plus lifeguards make this one of Oahu's most toddler-friendly beach spots.

shopping.name: Ala Moana Center
shopping.note: The world's largest open-air shopping center (350+ shops, ranked #2 shopping center in the US in USA Today's 2026 readers' poll) sits directly across the street from the beach park, making a beach-to-shopping stroll effortless.

museum.name: Bishop Museum
museum.note: Hawaii's largest museum runs a planetarium with family shows most days of the week (Tue, Thu-Sun) plus hands-on keiki (kids) LEGO workshops and family-friendly evening events.

outdoor.name: Zilker Park (Barton Springs Pool)
outdoor.note: This 358-acre park anchors Austin's outdoor family scene with a spring-fed swimming pool, a playscape, and the kid-favorite Zilker Zephyr mini-train ride.

shopping.name: South Congress Avenue (SoCo)
shopping.note: A walkable strip of quirky, family-friendly boutiques and toy/gift shops, plus the famous 'I love you so much' mural, makes for an easy, photogenic family stroll.

museum.name: Thinkery
museum.note: Austin's dedicated children's museum offers permanent hands-on exhibits (Train Town, a pretend Fresh! Farmers Market, a water-play zone called Currents) plus a large outdoor playground built specifically for kids.

confidence_notes: Austin is landlocked, so the outdoor pick is a park/springs rather than a beach, per instructions. Note Barton Springs Pool water stays a cool ~68-70°F year-round, which suits older toddlers and kids better than infants; the surrounding Zilker Park (playground, mini-train, green space) works well for all ages.

outdoor.name: Alki Beach
outdoor.note: A flat, 2.5-mile stroller-friendly promenade along Puget Sound with sandy beach play, a popular nearby playground ("whale tail park"), and summer lifeguards makes this West Seattle beach very family-manageable.

shopping.name: Pike Place Market
shopping.note: The iconic 1907 farmers market offers produce stalls, fish-tossing fishmongers, and kid-favorite stops (Rachel the Piggy Bank, mini doughnuts) that make for an engaging family stroll.

museum.name: Pacific Science Center
museum.note: This Seattle Center landmark runs a toddler-specific "Just for Tots" exhibit, a Tropical Butterfly House, live science shows, and planetarium/laser shows, giving families both interactive exhibits and scheduled programming.

confidence_notes: Seattle Children's Museum (also at Seattle Center) was separately confirmed open in 2026 as a strong alternate museum pick if a pure children's-museum format is preferred over a science center.
